1523.text:
Assertion : Generally the path of a projectile from the earth is parabolic but it is elliptical for projectiles going to a very great height.
Reason : Up to ordinary height the projectile moves under a uniform gravitational force, but for great heights, projectile moves under a variable force.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1523.sol: Upto ordinary heights the change in the distance of a projectile from the centre of the earth is negligible compared to the radius of the earth. Hence projectile moves under a nearly uniform gravitational force and its path is parabolic. But for projectiles going to great heights, the gravitational force decreases in inverse poroportion to the square of the distance of the projectile from the centre of the earth. Under such a variable force the path of projectile is elliptical.

3840.subject: Chemistry
3840.text: The correct order of acidic strength among the following is
3840.sol:
Acidity is directly proportional to the $- I, - M$ effect. The $- I$ effect of the fluorine atom is higher than the chlorine atom. So, the ${FCH}_{2}{CO}_{2}H$ has more acidity than the ${CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{CHClCO}_{2}H$. The benzoic acid has more acidic strength than the acetic acid because phenyl group show the $- I$ effect but methyl group will show the $+ I$ effect.

So, the acidity order is :-

${FCH}_{2}{CO}_{2}H > {CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{CHClCO}_{2}H > {C}_{6}{H}_{5}{CO}_{2}H > {CH}_{3}{CO}_{2}H$

15782.text: A particle is projected with velocity $2 \sqrt{g h}$, so that it just flies over two walls of equal height $h$ and $2 h$ distance apart from each other. Find the time for which the particle flies between the walls.
15782.sol:
Velocity of projection, $\begin{aligned}v & =2 \sqrt{g h}\\
\therefore \quad v_x & =v \cos \theta=2 \sqrt{g h} \cos \theta
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Time taken by the projectile to cover interwall distance, $\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{2 h}{v_x}=\frac{2 h}{2 \sqrt{g h} \cos \theta}\\
\Rightarrow \quad t & =\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}} \cdot \sec \theta
\end{aligned}$ Vertical velocity at the top of the wall is given as $\begin{aligned}v_y^{\prime 2} & =v_y^2-2 g h=(\sqrt{2 g h} \sin \theta)^2-2 g h \\
& =4 g h \sin ^2 \theta-2 g h \\
v_y^{\prime 2} & =2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right) \\
\therefore \quad v_y^{\prime} & =\sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}\\
& t=\frac{2 v_y^{\prime}}{g}\\
t & =\frac{2 \sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}}{g}
\end{aligned}$ From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}} \sec \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}}{g}$ Squaring both side, $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \frac{h}{g} \sec ^2 \theta=\frac{4 \times 2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}{g^2}\\
& \Rightarrow 1=8 \cos ^2 \theta\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 1=8 \cos ^2 \theta\left[2\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)-1\right]
\end{aligned} $\begin{array}{cc}
\Rightarrow& 16 $\cos ^4 \theta-8 \cos ^2 \theta+1=0$ \\
& $\left(4 $\cos ^2 \theta-1\right)^2$=0 \\
\Rightarrow & $\cos ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{4}$\\
\Rightarrow & $\cos \theta=\frac{1}{2}$=$\cos60^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}
\end{array} \therefore From $Eq. (i), t=\sqrt{$\frac{h}{g}}$\sec60^{{}^{\circ}}=\sqrt{$\frac{h}{g}}$\cdot2=\sqrt{$\frac{4 h}{g}$}

19573.subject: Chemistry
19573.text: Find the final product for the reaction
19573.sol:
The reaction between benzaldehyde (C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) and acetophenone (C_{6}H_{5}COCH_{3}$) in the presence of a base (OH^{-}$) is a classic Claisen-Schmidt condensation reaction.

Acetophenone acts as the nucleophile because it has \alpha$-hydrogens, which are removed by the base to form an enolate ion. Benzaldehyde acts as the electrophile because it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The enolate ion of acetophenone attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde to form a $\beta$-hydroxy ketone intermediate, which subsequently undergoes dehydration in the presence of the base and heat to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product formed is benzalacetophenone (also known as chalcone), which has the structure $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CO-C_{6}H_{5}$.

Comparing this structure with the given options, the first option matches the structure of chalcone.

Answer:

20150.subject: Chemistry
20150.text:
$\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ undergoes disproportionation, according to the equation,
$
2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{Cu}
$
The $\mathrm{E}^{{}^{\circ}}$ value for the reaction is:
$[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}^{\mathrm{o}}=0.34 \mathrm{ V} \text{ and } \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}^{+}}^{\mathrm{O}}=0.15 \mathrm{ V}]$
20150.sol:
The given disproportionation reaction is $2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + \mathrm{Cu}$.

This reaction can be split into two half-reactions:
1) Oxidation: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-}$ (where $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{ox} = -E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}^{+}} = -0.15 \text{ V}$)
2) Reduction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$ (where $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{red} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$)

To find $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$, we use the Gibbs free energy relation $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -nFE^{{}^{\circ}}$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{1} = -2 \times F \times 0.34 = -0.68F$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{2} = -1 \times F \times 0.15 = -0.15F$.
Subtracting the second from the first gives $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, with $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} = \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{1} - \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{2} = -0.68F - (-0.15F) = -0.53F$.
Thus, $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}} = -\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} / (1 \times F) = 0.53 \text{ V}$.

The standard cell potential for the disproportionation reaction is $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{cell} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{ox} + E^{{}^{\circ}}_{red} = -0.15 \text{ V} + 0.53 \text{ V} = +0.38 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $+0.38$ V

21247.subject: Mathematics
21247.text: $\int_0^\pi \dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x}} d x$ is equal to
21247.sol:
Let $I = \int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}} dx$.

Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) dx = \int_0^a f(a-x) dx$, we have:

$I = \int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{e^{\cos(\pi-x)}}{e^{\cos(\pi-x)} + e^{-\cos(\pi-x)}} dx$

Since $\cos(\pi-x) = -\cos x$, the integral becomes:

$I = \int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{e^{-\cos x}}{e^{-\cos x} + e^{\cos x}} dx$

Adding the two expressions for $I$:

$2I = \int_0^{\pi} \left( \dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}} + \dfrac{e^{-\cos x}}{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}} \right) dx$

$2I = \int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}}{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}} dx$

$2I = \int_0^{\pi} 1 dx = \pi$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

21534.subject: Mathematics
21534.text: The corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints are $(0,3),(1,1)$ and $(3,0)$. If objective function is $Z=p x+q y, p, q > 0$ then the condition on $p$ and $q$ so that the minimum of $Z$ occurs at $(3,0)$ and $(1,1)$ is
21534.sol:
The objective function is $Z = px + qy$.

The values of $Z$ at the corner points are:
At $(0,3)$, $Z = p(0) + q(3) = 3q$.
At $(1,1)$, $Z = p(1) + q(1) = p + q$.
At $(3,0)$, $Z = p(3) + q(0) = 3p$.

For the minimum of $Z$ to occur at both $(3,0)$ and $(1,1)$, the values of $Z$ at these two points must be equal, and this value must be less than or equal to the value at the third corner point $(0,3)$.

Equating the values at $(3,0)$ and $(1,1)$:
$3p = p + q$
$2p = q$
$p = \dfrac{q}{2}$

Checking the condition at $(0,3)$ with $q = 2p$:
$Z(3,0) = 3p$
$Z(1,1) = p + 2p = 3p$
$Z(0,3) = 3(2p) = 6p$

Since $p > 0$, $3p < 6p$, which confirms that the minimum value $3p$ is indeed attained at $(3,0)$ and $(1,1)$.

Thus, the condition is $p = \dfrac{q}{2}$.

Answer: $p=\dfrac{q}{2}$

23027.subject: Physics
23027.text:
A wire of length $2 \mathrm{ m}$ carries a current of $1 \mathrm{ A}$ along the $\mathrm{x}$ axis. A magnetic field $B=B_0(i+j+k)$ tesla exists in space.
The magnitude of magnetic force on the wire is
23027.sol:
The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is given by the formula $\vec{F} = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})$.

The length vector $\vec{L}$ of the wire is $2\hat{i}$ m, as it lies along the x-axis and has a length of $2$ m. The current $I$ is $1$ A.

The magnetic field is given as $\vec{B} = B_0(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$.

Substituting these values into the force equation:
$\vec{F} = 1 \times (2\hat{i}) \times B_0(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$
$\vec{F} = 2B_0 [(\hat{i} \times \hat{i}) + (\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + (\hat{i} \times \hat{k})]$

Using the cross product properties $\hat{i} \times \hat{i} = 0$, $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, and $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$:
$\vec{F} = 2B_0 [0 + \hat{k} - \hat{j}] = 2B_0(\hat{k} - \hat{j})$

The magnitude of the force is $|\vec{F}| = |2B_0| \sqrt{(1)^2 + (-1)^2} = 2B_0 \sqrt{2}$.

Answer: 2$\sqrt2$ B_0$ N$

26189.text: A charge $q$ is surrounded by a closed surface consisting of an inverted cone of height $h$ and base radius $R$, and a hemisphere of radius $R$ as shown in the figure. The electric flux through the conical surface is$\dfrac{nq}{6{ε}_{0}}$ (in $SI$ units). The value of $n$ is _________.
26189.sol:
According to the Gauss law, the total flux linked with a closed surface is $\dfrac{1}{{ε}_{0}}$ times the charge enclosed by the closed surface.

As we can see from the diagram, the given shape encloses the charge $q$, therefore from Gauss law, we can write total flux $= \dfrac{q}{{ε}_{0}}$.

Now, the plane connecting hemispherical shape & conical shape cuts the charge in two equal parts, therefore flux through the conical part will be exactly half of the total flux value.

Hence, flux through conical part is, $\dfrac{q}{2{ε}_{0}}$.

Therefore,

$n = 3$

27843.text: Identify the incorrect statement for ${PCl}_{5}$ from the following.
options: In this molecule, orbitals of phosphorous are assumed to undergo ${sp}^{3}d$ hybridization.
The geometry of ${PCl}_{5}$ is trigonal bipyramidal.
${PCl}_{5}$ has two axial bonds stronger than three equatorial bonds.
The three equatorial bonds of ${PCl}_{5}$ lie in a plane.
27843.sol:
sp3d hybridization is shown in phosphorus penta chloride (PCl5). The grounds state and the excited state outer electronic configurations of phosphorus (Z=15) are represented below

Now the five orbitals (i.e., one s, three p and one d orbitals) are available for hybridization to yield a set of five sp3d hybrid orbitals which are directed towards the five corners of a trigonal bipyramidal as depicted in the below.

It should be noted that tall the bond angles in trigonal bipyramidal geometry are not equivalent. In PCl5 the five sp3d orbitals of phosphorus overlap with the singly occupied p orbitals of chlorine atoms to form five P-Cl sigma bonds. Three P-Cl bond lie in one plane and make an angle of 120o with each other; these bonds are termed as equatorial bonds. The remaining two P-Cl bonds-one lying above and the other lying below the equatorial plane, make an angle of 90o with the plane. These bonds are called axial bonds. As the axial bond pairs suffer more repulsive interaction form the equatorial bond pairs, therefore axial bonds have been found to be slightly longer and hence slightly weaker than the equatorial bonds; which makes PCl5 molecule more reactive.

30402.subject: Chemistry
30402.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions to give the major product $(X)$

$P$ g of the major product $(X)$ formed is reacted with $NaHCO_3$ solution to liberate a gas which occupied $11.2$ dm$^3$ at STP. $P = $ _____ g. (Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H:$1$, C:$12$, O:$16$, Cl:$35.5$)
30402.sol:
Step 1: The first reaction is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation. Benzene reacts with $CH_3Cl$ in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ to form toluene.

Step 2: The second reaction is electrophilic aromatic substitution. Toluene reacts with $Cl_2$ in the presence of $FeCl_3$ to form a mixture of o-chlorotoluene and p-chlorotoluene. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is p-chlorotoluene.

Step 3: The third reaction is the oxidation of the alkyl side chain. p-chlorotoluene is oxidized by $K_2Cr_2O_7 / H_2SO_4$ to form p-chlorobenzoic acid, which is the major product $(X)$.

The molecular formula of p-chlorobenzoic acid is $C_7H_5ClO_2$.
Molar mass of $(X) = (7 \times 12) + (5 \times 1) + 35.5 + (2 \times 16) = 84 + 5 + 35.5 + 32 = 156.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Step 4: Reaction of p-chlorobenzoic acid with $NaHCO_3$ liberates $CO_2$ gas:
$C_6H_4ClCOOH + NaHCO_3 \rightarrow C_6H_4ClCOONa + H_2O + CO_2 \uparrow$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of p-chlorobenzoic acid produces $1$ mole of $CO_2$ gas.
Volume of $CO_2$ liberated at STP = $11.2 \text{ dm}^3$.
Moles of $CO_2$ liberated = $\dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5 \text{ mol}$.

Therefore, moles of p-chlorobenzoic acid reacted = $0.5 \text{ mol}$.
Mass of $(X)$ reacted, $P = 0.5 \text{ mol} \times 156.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 78.25 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $78.25$

36399.text: The number of ways, in which $5$ girls and $7$ boys can be seated at a round  table so that no two girls sit together is
36399.sol:
Given,

$7$ boys and $5$ girls are to be seated around a circular such that no two girls to be seated together,

Now we know that $n$ objects can be arranged in a circle in $( n - 1 ) !$ ways.

Let us first arrange $7$ boys in circular arrangement in $\left(7 - 1\right) !$ ways.

Now there will be $7$ gaps.

So let us select any $5$ gaps out of $7$ gaps and arrange $5$ girls in the chosen gaps. This can be done in $C5 7 \times 5 !$ ways.

Hence, required arrangements are $6 ! \times C5 7 \times 5 !

$= 6 \times 5 ! \times $\dfrac{7 \times 6}{2}$ \times 5 !

$= 126{\left(5 !\right)}^{2}$.

Therefore, required arrangements are $126{\left(5 !\right)}^{2}$

36452.text: The sum of all the elements in the set ${ n \in { 1, 2, \ldots \ldots , 100 } ∣$ H.C.F. of $n$ and $2040$ is $1$} is equal to __________.
36452.sol:
The prime factorisation of the given number is $2040 = {2}^{3} \times 3 \times 5 \times 17$

The H.C.F. of $n$ and $2040$ is $1$ if $n$ is not a multiple of $2, 3, 5$ and $17 .$

Hence $n$ cannot be multiple of $2, 3, 5$ and $17$

Then sum is $n ( 1 ) - ( n ( 2 ) + n ( 3 ) + n ( 5 ) + n ( 17 ) - n ( 6 ) - n ( 10 ) - n ( 34 ) - n ( 15 ) - n ( 51 ) - n ( 85 ) ) + n ( 30 ) )$
Where $n ( a )$ means the sum of all numbers belonging to the set ${ 1, 2, \ldots \ldots . 100 }$ which are divisible by $a$

$= \dfrac{100 \times 101}{2} - \left(\dfrac{2 \times 50 \times 51}{2} + \dfrac{3 \times 33 \times 34}{2} + \dfrac{5 \times 20 \times 21}{2} + \dfrac{17 \times 5 \times 6}{2} - \dfrac{6 \times 16 \times 17}{2} - \dfrac{10 \times 10 \times 11}{2} - \dfrac{34 \times 2 \times 3}{2} - \dfrac{15 \times 6 \times 7}{2} - 51 - 85 + 180\right)$

$= 5050 - 2550 - 1683 - 1050 - 255 + 816 + 550 + 102 + 315 + 51 + 85 - 180$

$= 1251$

Alternate Solution:
Thus, the sum of all the required numbers taking the common elements only once, is $\left(1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots . . + 99\right) - \left(3 + 9 + 15 + 21 + \ldots \ldots + 99\right) - \left(5 + 25 + 35 + 55 + 65 + 85 + 95\right) - \left(17\right)$

Now, using the sum of $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression i.e. ${S}_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[a + l\right],$ where $a$ is the first term and $l$ is the last term.

$= \dfrac{50}{2}\left[1 + 99\right] - \dfrac{17}{2}\left[3 + 99\right] - \left(365\right) - 17$

$= \dfrac{50}{2}\left(100\right) - \dfrac{17}{2}\left(102\right) - 365 - 17$

$= 2500 - 867 - 365 - 17$

$= 1251 .$

43156.subject: Physics
43156.text: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{J}.\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
43156.sol:
Let the mass of the flywheel be $M = 3$ kg and its radius be $R = 5$ m.
Let the hanging mass be $m = 3$ kg and the distance descended be $h = 3$ m.
The flywheel is a disk, so its moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
By conservation of energy, the loss in potential energy of the hanging mass equals the gain in kinetic energy of the system.
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$
Since the string does not slip, $v = R\omega$, so $\omega = \frac{v}{R}$.
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}MR^2)(\frac{v}{R})^2$
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{4}Mv^2$
Substituting the values: $3 \times 10 \times 3 = \frac{1}{2}(3)v^2 + \frac{1}{4}(3)v^2$
$90 = \frac{3}{2}v^2 + \frac{3}{4}v^2 = \frac{9}{4}v^2$
$v^2 = \frac{90 \times 4}{9} = 40$ m$^2$/s$^2$.
The kinetic energy of the wheel is $K_{wheel} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{4}Mv^2$.
$K_{wheel} = \frac{1}{4} \times 3 \times 40 = 30$ J.

The formula to calculate the current gain $\left(\beta\right)$ in CE configuration is given by

$\beta = \dfrac{∆ {I}_{C}}{∆ {I}_{B}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Considering the third and the first points on the given graph, the current gain can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\beta & = & \dfrac{\left(30 - 10\right) \times {10}^{- 3}A}{\left(300 - 100\right) \times {10}^{- 6}A} \\ & = & 100\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the power gain $\left(P\right)$ in CE mode can be written as

$P = {\beta}^{2} \cdot \dfrac{{R}_{C}}{{R}_{B}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the known values of the parameters into equation (2) and solve to calculate the required unknown parameter.

$\begin{cases}{10}^{x} & = & {100}^{2} \times \dfrac{1kΩ}{10kΩ} \\ & = & 1000 \\ & = & {10}^{3} \\ & ⇒ & x = 3\end{cases}$

46095.text: A small disc of radius 2 cm is cut from a disc of radius 6 cm . If the distance between their centres is 3.2 cm , what is the shift in the centre of mass of the disc?
46095.sol: The situation can be shown as : Let radius of complete disc is $a$ and that of small disc is $b$. Also let centre of mass now shifts to $\mathrm{O}_2$ at a distance $x_2$ from original centre. The position of new centre of mass is given by $X_{\mathrm{CM}}=\frac{-\sigma \cdot \pi b^2 \cdot x_1}{\sigma \cdot \pi a^2-\sigma \cdot \pi b^2}$ Here, $a=6 \mathrm{~cm}, b=2 \mathrm{~cm}, x_1=3.2 \mathrm{~cm}$ Hence, $\quad X_{\mathrm{CM}}=\frac{-\sigma \times \pi(2)^2 \times 3.2}{\sigma \times \pi \times(6)^2-\sigma \times \pi \times(2)^2} \begin{aligned} & =\frac{12.8 \pi}{32 \pi} \\ & =-0.4 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

46314.text: A electron $\left(\mathrm{e}^{-}\right)$is accelerated by V volts experiences a force F , when it enters in a uniform magnetic field. What will the force experienced when it is accelerated by 2 V ?
46314.sol:
When $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is accelerated by V volts, then work done by $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is equals to kinetic energy of $\mathrm{e}^{-}$.
or $\quad \mathrm{qV}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2$
Then, the velocity of $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{qV}}{\mathrm{m}}}$ or $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{\mathrm{V}}$. When $\mathrm{e}^{-}$accelerated by V volts, then $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{\mathrm{V}}$.
Force experiences by $\mathrm{e}^{-}$in a uniform magnetic field, $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qvB}$
or $\quad \mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qk} \sqrt{\mathrm{V} B}$   ...(i)
When e accelerated by 2 V volts, then $\mathrm{v}_1=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{2 \mathrm{~V}}$.
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{F}_1=\mathrm{qv}_1 \mathrm{~B}=\mathrm{qk} \sqrt{2 \mathrm{VB}}$
Hence, $\quad \mathrm{F}_1=\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~F} \quad$ [from Eq. (i)]

46637.text: Which of the following circular rods, (given radius $r$ and length $l$) each made of the same material and whose ends are maintained at the same temperature will conduct most heat?
46637.sol:
Heat conduction through a rod is rate of change of heat $\left(\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}\right)$.
$\therefore H=\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}=K A\left(\frac{T_1-T_2}{l}\right) \Rightarrow H \propto \frac{r^2}{l}...(i)$
(a) When
$\begin{aligned} r & =2 r_0, l=2 l_0 \\ H & \propto \frac{\left(2 r_0\right)^2}{2l_0} \Rightarrow H \propto \frac{2 r_0^2}{l_0}\end{aligned}$
(b) When 
$\begin{aligned} r & =2 r_0, l=l_0 \\ H & \propto \frac{\left(2 r_0\right)^2}{ l_0} \Rightarrow H \propto \frac{4 r_0^2}{l_0}\end{aligned}$
(c) When
$\begin{gathered}r=r_0, l=l_0 \\ H \propto \frac{r_0^2}{l_0}\end{gathered}$
(d) When
$\begin{aligned} r & =r_0, l=2 l_0 \\ H & \propto \frac{r_0^2}{2 l_0}\end{aligned}$
It is obvious that heat conduction will be more in case (b).

47348.subject: Chemistry
47348.text:
Match the reagents in List-I with products obtained from their carbonyl compounds in List-II.
List-IList-II
(a)$NH_2OH$(i)Cyanohydrin
(b)$R-NH_2$(ii)Oxime
(c)$R-OH$(iii)Schiff base
(d)$H-C \equiv N$(iv)Acetal
47348.sol:
Reaction of carbonyl compounds with various reagents yields specific products:

(a) Reaction with hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$) forms an oxime.
$\text{C=O} + \text{NH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{C=N-OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(b) Reaction with a primary amine ($R-\text{NH}_2$) forms a substituted imine, also known as a Schiff base.
$\text{C=O} + R-\text{NH}_2 \rightarrow \text{C=N}-R + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(c) Reaction with an alcohol ($R-\text{OH}$) in the presence of dry HCl gas forms a hemiacetal, which further reacts with another molecule of alcohol to form an acetal.
$\text{RCHO} + 2R'\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OR')}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(d) Reaction with hydrogen cyanide ($\text{HCN}$) forms a cyanohydrin.
$\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{C(OH)(CN)}$

Thus, the correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

Answer: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i

(b)$B_2$(ii)RBC deficiency in haemoglobin

47424.sol:
According to the biochemical functions and deficiency diseases of vitamins:

Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beri-beri, which is characterized by loss of appetite and retarded growth. Thus, (a) matches with (iii).

Vitamin $\text{B}_2$ (Riboflavin) deficiency causes Cheilosis, digestive disorders, and a burning sensation of the skin. Thus, (b) matches with (iv).

Vitamin $\text{B}_6$ (Pyridoxine) deficiency causes convulsions. Thus, (c) matches with (i).

Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ (Cyanocobalamin) deficiency causes pernicious anaemia, which is characterized by RBCs deficient in haemoglobin. Thus, (d) matches with (ii).

The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

Answer: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii

47827.text:
How many Coulombs of electricity are required for the oxidation of one mol of water to
dioxygen?
47827.sol:
For the oxidation of one mole of water to dioxygen,
\( \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}+2 e^{-} \)
\( 2 \mathrm{~F} \) Coulombs of electricity is required.
Therefore, electricity in \( \mathrm{C} \) is
\[ \begin{array}{l} =2 \times F \\ =2 \times 96500 \\ =193000 C \\ =1.93 \times 10^{5} C \end{array} \]

50032.subject: Physics
50032.text: The additional energy that should be given to an electron to reduce its de-Broglie wavelength from $1 \mathrm{ nm}$ to $0.5 \mathrm{ nm}$ is
50032.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength,
$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E_{k}}} \quad \therefore \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{E_{k}}}$
(\because$ h and $m$ remains constant)
Here, in given condition
\begin{array}{ll}
\frac{\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{E_{k_{2}}}{E_{k_{1}}}}, \quad \frac{\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 E}{E}} \\
\lambda_{1}=2 \lambda_{2}, & \lambda_{2}=\frac{\lambda_{1}}{2}
\end{array}
So, if $ E_{k}$ is increased by four times, then \lambda$ becomes half.
$\therefore$ Additional kinetic energy that should be supplied to the electron
$=4 E_{k}-E_{k}=3 E_{k}$

54841.subject: Chemistry
54841.text:
Select the correct decreasing order of acid strength for the following compounds.
a) Ethanol b) 2-Methyl propan-2-ol c) Phenol d) p - Nitrophenol
54841.sol:
Acid strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base formed after the removal of an $H^+$ ion.

The conjugate bases are:
a) Ethoxide ion ($CH_3CH_2O^-$)
b) tert-Butoxide ion ($(CH_3)_3CO^-$)
c) Phenoxide ion ($C_6H_5O^-$)
d) p-Nitrophenoxide ion ($p-NO_2-C_6H_4O^-$)

Phenoxide ions are resonance stabilized, making phenols more acidic than aliphatic alcohols. Thus, (c) and (d) are more acidic than (a) and (b).

In p-nitrophenol (d), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-I$ and $-R$ effects, which further stabilizes the phenoxide ion. Hence, p-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol (c).

Among the alcohols, the $+I$ effect of the alkyl groups destabilizes the alkoxide ion. The tert-butyl group in 2-methylpropan-2-ol (b) exerts a stronger $+I$ effect than the ethyl group in ethanol (a). Therefore, ethanol is more acidic than 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

The correct decreasing order of acid strength is d > c > a > b.

Answer: d > c > a > b

56447.subject: Chemistry
56447.text: $What is the number of unpaired electrons in \left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ complex?
56447.sol:
The cobalt ion in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ has an oxidation state of +3, giving it the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6$.

Ammonia is a strong field ligand that causes significant crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes. This favors electron pairing in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals before occupying $e_g$ orbitals.

All six electrons pair completely in the three $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $\uparrow\downarrow \uparrow\downarrow \uparrow\downarrow$

There are zero unpaired electrons.

56837.subject: Chemistry
56837.text: The standard potential of $\text{Cu}^{+2}/\text{Cu}$ is $0.34$ V at $298$ K. Calculate its potential at the same temperature when the $\text{Cu}^{+2}$ ion concentration is $0.1$ M.
56837.sol:
The reduction half-reaction is $\text{Cu}^{+2} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Cu}$.

Using the Nernst equation for the electrode potential:

$E = E^{{}^{\circ}} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{1}{[\text{Cu}^{+2}]}$

Given $E^{{}^{\circ}} = 0.34$ V, $n = 2$, and $[\text{Cu}^{+2}] = 0.1$ M.

$E = 0.34 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{1}{0.1}$

$E = 0.34 - 0.0295 \log 10$

$E = 0.34 - 0.0295 \times 1$

$E = 0.3105$ V $\approx 0.31$ V.

Answer: $0.31$ V

56848.text: What is reduction potential of hydrogen gas electrode when pure hydrogen gas is at 1 atmospheric pressure and platinum electrode is in contact with HCl solution of PH 1 at 298 K ?
56848.sol:
The reduction potential for the hydrogen electrode under specified conditions is determined using the Nernst equation:

$E_{red} = E^0_{red} - \frac{0.0592}{n} \log \frac{P_{H_2}}{[H^+]^2}$

Substituting $E^0_{red} = 0 \text{ V}$, $P_{H_2} = 1 \text{ atm}$, and $n = 2$, with $[H^+] = 10^{-\text{pH}} = 10^{-1} \text{ M}$, yields:

$E_{red} = - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log \frac{1}{(10^{-1})^2} = - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log(10^2)$

Simplifying the logarithmic term, $\log(10^2) = 2$, results in:

$E_{red} = -0.0592 \text{ V}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

57575.subject: Chemistry
57575.text: Which of the following alkyl halides is hydrolyzed most rapidly by the $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism ?
57575.sol:
The rate of an $\text{SN}^2$ reaction is inversely proportional to the steric hindrance around the carbon atom bearing the leaving group.

The order of reactivity of alkyl halides towards $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism is:
Methyl halide $ > 1^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide $ > 2^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide $ > 3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide.

Among the given options:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$ is a methyl halide.
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-Br}$ is a $1^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide.
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-Br}$ is a $2^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide.
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br}$ is a $3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide.

Since $\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$ has the least steric hindrance, it is hydrolyzed most rapidly by the $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$

57760.subject: Chemistry
57760.text: Which of the following alkanes is NOT obtained when a mixture of ethyl iodide and n-propyl iodide is subjected to Wurtz reaction?
57760.sol:
In the Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides react with sodium in dry ether to form alkanes through the coupling of alkyl radicals.

The given mixture contains ethyl iodide (C_2H_5I$) and n-propyl iodide (C_3H_7I$). The free radicals generated are the ethyl radical (C_2H_5^{\bullet}$) and the n-propyl radical (C_3H_7^{\bullet}$).

The possible coupling products are:
1. Self-coupling of ethyl radicals:
$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_4H_{10}$ (n-Butane)

2. Cross-coupling of ethyl and n-propyl radicals:
$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_3H_7^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_5H_{12}$ (n-Pentane)

3. Self-coupling of n-propyl radicals:
$C_3H_7^{\bullet} + C_3H_7^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_6H_{14}$ (n-Hexane)

Propane (C_3H_8$) would require the coupling of a methyl radical (CH_3^{\bullet}$) and an ethyl radical (C_2H_5^{\bullet}$). Since methyl iodide is not present in the mixture, propane is not obtained as a coupling product.

Answer: Propane$

2$\left(\mathrm{x}^$2-1\right)=0 \Rightarrow $\mathrm{x}= \pm$1

60728.subject: Mathematics
60728.text: The least distance of the point $A(10,7)$ from the circle $x^2+\mathrm{y}^2-4 x-2 \mathrm{y}-20=0$ is length of seg. AM. If $\mathrm{MM}^{\prime}$ is the diameter of the circle, then the lengths of AM and $\mathrm{AM}^{\prime}$ are respectively _______ , ______ units
60728.sol:
The given circle $x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 2y - 20 = 0$ has center $(2,1)$ and radius $5$ units.
For point $A(10,7)$, the distance from the center is $AC = \sqrt{(10-2)^2 + (7-1)^2} = 10$ units.

Since $AC > r$, point $A$ lies outside the circle.

60903.text: Let $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x and $f(x) = [\tan^2 x]$, then which of the following is true ?
60903.sol:
For $x \in (-\pi/4, \pi/4)$, we have $-1 < \tan x < 1$.

Squaring both sides, we get $0 \le \tan^2 x < 1$.

Therefore, $f(x) = [\tan^2 x] = 0$ for all $x \in (-\pi/4, \pi/4)$.

Since $f(x) = 0$ in a neighborhood of $x = 0$, we have $\lim\limits_{x \to 0} f(x) = 0$ and $f(0) = 0$.

Thus, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$.

Furthermore, since $f(x)$ is constant in this neighborhood, $f'(0) = 0$, meaning $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 0$.

Answer: $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$

61667.text: If $y = \log x^x$, then the value of $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ at $x = e^2$ is
61667.sol:
Given $y = \log x^x$

Using the property of logarithms, this can be written as:

$y = x \log x$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$ using the product rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} + \log x \cdot 1$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \log x$

Substituting $x = e^2$ into the derivative:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \log(e^2)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + 2\log e$

Since $\log e = 1$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + 2 = 3$

Therefore, the value of $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ is:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9$

Answer: $9$

Since $x = \sin t$, we have $t = \arcsin x$ for $t \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]$,

The first derivative is $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{p \cos(p \arcsin x)}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
Multiplying both sides by $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ gives $\sqrt{1-x^2} \frac{dy}{dx} = p \cos(p \arcsin x)$.

Squaring both sides yields $(1-x^2) \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = p^2 \cos^2(p \arcsin x)$.
Using $\cos^2 \theta = 1 - \sin^2 \theta$,
this becomes $(1-x^2) \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = p^2 (1 - y^2)$.

$-2x \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 2(1-x^2)\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -2p^2 y \frac{dy}{dx}$.

Dividing through by $2\frac{dy}{dx}$ (with $\frac{dy}{dx} \neq 0$)
and rearranging terms produces the final expression:

$\left(1-x^2\right) \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}-x \frac{d y}{d x}+p^2 y = 0$.

The expression evaluates to $\boxed{A}$.

66549.text: Light of wavelength '$\lambda$' which is less than threshold wavelength is incident on a photosensitive material. If incident wavelength is decreased so that emitted photoelectrons are moving with some velocity then stopping potential
66549.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by

$K_{\max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

where $\lambda$ is the incident wavelength and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

The stopping potential $V_s$ is related to the maximum kinetic energy by

$eV_s = K_{\max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

When the incident wavelength $\lambda$ is decreased, the term $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$ increases. Since the work function $\Phi$ remains constant for a given material, the maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ of the photoelectrons increases.

Consequently, the stopping potential $V_s$ also increases.

Answer: increases

de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is the following ratio: $\lambda=\frac{h}{P}$
Therefore, on tripling the kinetic energy the wavelength will change to: $\lambda^{\prime}=\frac{h}{P^{\prime}}=\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{h}{P}\right)=\sqrt{3} \lambda$

67300.text: The depth below the earth's surface at which the acceleration due to gravity ' $g$ ' becomes $\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{n}}$ is $(\mathrm{R}=$ radius of the earth, $\mathrm{n}$ is an integer, $\mathrm{n} > 1)$

At a depth $\mathrm{h}$ below the surface, considering force balance:

& \Rightarrow \frac{R-h}{R}=\frac{1}{n} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{-h}{R}=\frac{1-n}{n}
\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=\frac{(\mathrm{n}-1) \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{n}}$

68124.text: The surface of water in a water tank of cross-section area $750$ cm^2$ on the top of a house is $h$ m above the tap level. By the equation of continuity, $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$.

Here, $A_1 = 750 \text{ cm}^2$, $A_2 = 500 \text{ mm}^2 = 5 \text{ cm}^2$, and $v_2 = 30 \text{ cm/s}$.

Converting to m/s, $v_1 = 0.2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m/s} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/s}$.

Since $v_1 = \dfrac{dh}{dt}$, we have $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/s}$.

Comparing with $y \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/s}$, we get $y = 2$.

Answer: $2$

The equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid in steady flow requires that the mass flow rate remains constant, thus $A_A V_A = A_B V_B$.

The cross-sectional area varies with the square of the radius: $A_A = \pi R^2$ and $A_B = \pi \left(\frac{R}{3}\right)^2 = \pi \frac{R^2}{9}$.

Substituting into the continuity equation gives $\pi R^2 V = \pi \frac{R^2}{9} V_B$.

Solving for $V_B$ by canceling $\pi R^2$ yields $V_B = 9V$.

Final answer: $\boxed{9V}$

68969.subject: Physics
68969.text: A ray of light travelling through rarer medium is incident at a very small angle 'i' on a glass slab and after refraction its velocity is reduced by $20 \%$. The angle of deviation is
68969.sol:
Let the velocity of light in air be $v_1$ and in glass be $v_2$, with corresponding refractive indices $n_1 = 1$ and $n_2$. The velocity decreases by 20%, so $v_2 = 0.8v_1$.

Using the relation $n \propto 1/v$, we have $\frac{n_1}{n_2} = \frac{v_2}{v_1} = 0.8$. Solving gives $n_2 = \frac{1}{0.8} = \frac{5}{4}$.

Snell's law states $n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$. For small angles, $\sin \theta \approx \theta$, so $i = \frac{5}{4}r$ and $r = \frac{4}{5}i$.

The deviation is $\delta = i - r = i - \frac{4}{5}i = \frac{1}{5}i$.

69126.text: The critical angle for light going from medium ‘x’ to medium ‘y’ is $'{\theta}^{'}$. The speed of light in medium ‘x’ is $'{v}_x^{'}$. The speed of light in medium ‘y’ is

Where, $\mu =$ refractive index of medium.
$Also, \mu = \dfrac{speedoflightinvacuum}{speedoflightinmedium} = \dfrac{c}{v}$ … (ii)
Form Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$sin\theta\dfrac{c}{{v}_{y}} \times \dfrac{{v}_{x}}{c} = \dfrac{{v}_{x}}{{v}_{y}} ⇒ {v}_{y} = \dfrac{{v}_{x}}{sin\theta}$

69718.text: A black rectangular surface of area 'A' emits energy 'E' per second at $27^{}^{\circ}$ C. If length and breadth is reduced to half of its initial value and temperature is raised to $327^{}^{\circ}$ C then energy emitted per second becomes
69718.sol:

Initial area $A_1 = A$

Energy emitted per second $E = \sigma A T_1^4 = \sigma A (300)^4$

When length and breadth are reduced to half, the new area $A_2 = \dfrac{L}{2} \times \dfrac{B}{2} = \dfrac{A}{4}$

New temperature $T_2 = 327^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C} = 600\text{ K}$

New energy emitted per second $E' = \sigma A_2 T_2^4$

$E' = \sigma \left(\dfrac{A}{4}\right) (600)^4$

$E' = \sigma \left(\dfrac{A}{4}\right) (2 \times 300)^4$

$E' = \sigma \left(\dfrac{A}{4}\right) \times 16 \times (300)^4$

$E' = 4 \sigma A (300)^4 = 4E$

Answer: $4E$

69758.subject: Physics
69758.text: If a black body at 400 K surrounded by atmosphere at 300 K has rate of cooling ' $\mathrm{R}_0$ ', the same body at 900 K , surrounded by same atmosphere, will have rate of cooling nearly
69758.sol:
The rate of cooling for a black body due to radiation follows Stefan-Boltzmann's Law: $R = \epsilon \sigma A (T^4 - T_s^4)$, where $\epsilon = 1$ for a black body.

At initial temperature $T_1 = 400$ K with surroundings at $T_s = 300$ K, the cooling rate is $R_0 = \epsilon \sigma A (400^4 - 300^4) = \epsilon \sigma A \times 10^8 (256 - 81) = \epsilon \sigma A \times 10^8 \cdot 175$.

At temperature $T_2 = 900$ K with the same $T_s = 300$ K, the cooling rate becomes $R = \epsilon \sigma A (900^4 - 300^4) = \epsilon \sigma A \times 10^8 (6561 - 81) = \epsilon \sigma A \times 10^8 \cdot 6480$.

The ratio yields $\frac{R}{R_0} = \frac{6480}{175} = \frac{1296}{35} \approx 37.03$.

Among the given options, this value is closest to 36, indicating the rate of cooling will be nearly $36 R_0$.

70153.subject: Physics
70153.text: A double slit experiment is immersed in water of refractive index $1.33$. The slit separation is 1 mm, distance between slit and screen is $1.33$ m. The slits are illuminated by light of wavelength 6300 $\text{\AA}$. The fringe width is
70153.sol:
When the double slit experiment is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu$, the wavelength of light in the medium becomes $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$.

The fringe width $\beta$ is given by the formula:

$\beta = \dfrac{\lambda' D}{d} = \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$

Given values are:
$\lambda = 6300 \text{ \AA} = 6300 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$
$D = 1.33 \text{ m}$
$\mu = 1.33$
$d = 1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$\beta = \dfrac{6300 \times 10^{-10} \times 1.33}{1.33 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\beta = \dfrac{6300 \times 10^{-10}}{10^{-3}}$

$\beta = 6300 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$

$\beta = 6.3 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$

Answer: $6.3 \times 10^{-4}$ m

70208.subject: Physics
70208.text: In Young's double slit experiment, for the $n$ th dark fringe (n=1,2,3 \ldots$ ) the phase difference of the interfering waves in radian will be$
70208.sol:
The phase difference for the $n$ th dark fringe follows from the condition for destructive interference, where the path difference is $\Delta x = (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$ for $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$

Since phase difference relates to path difference by $\Delta \phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$, substituting gives $\Delta \phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \cdot (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$.
Simplifying yields $\Delta \phi = (2n - 1)\pi$ radians.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

Given $\mathrm{I}_1=2 \mathrm{I}_2\therefore \quad \frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\frac{3 \mathrm{I}_2+2 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{I}_2}{3 \mathrm{I}_2-2 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{I}_2}=\frac{3+2 \sqrt{2}}{3-2 \sqrt{2}}=34$

70975.subject: Biology
70975.text: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT based on the above graph showing the rate of enzyme action?
options: $\text{K}_m$ or Michaelis-Menten constant is the substrate concentration to produce half of the maximum velocity in an enzyme catalyzed reaction.
It shows that half of the enzyme molecules are bound with substrate molecules when substate concentration equals $\text{K}_m$ value.
A high $\text{K}_m$ value indicates a strong affinity between enzyme and substrate.
The maximum rate of an enzyme reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of enzymes.
70975.sol:
The Michaelis-Menten constant (K_m$) is defined as the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of its maximum velocity (V_\max/2$). This directly supports statement (1).

At $K_m$, the reaction rate is $V_\max/2$. This means that exactly half of the active sites on the enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate molecules. This supports statement (2).

The maximum rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction (V_\max$) is directly proportional to the total concentration of the enzyme present (V_\max = k_{cat} \times [E]_{total}$). This supports statement (4).

The $K_m$ value is an inverse measure of the affinity of an enzyme for its substrate. A lower $K_m$ value indicates that a lower concentration of substrate is needed to reach half the maximum velocity, meaning the enzyme has a high affinity for the substrate. Conversely, a high $K_m$ value indicates a weak affinity between the enzyme and the substrate, as more substrate is required to achieve $V_\max/2$. Therefore, statement (3) is incorrect.

Answer: A high $\text{K}_m$ value indicates a strong affinity between enzyme and substrate.

71335.subject: Biology
71335.text: The natural auxin produced by the placental tissue of the unfertilized ovary and responsible for enlargement of ovary into fruit is ---------------.
71335.sol:
Auxins are a class of plant hormones that play a crucial role in various aspects of plant growth and development.

Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is the principal natural auxin found in plants. It is produced by the placental tissue of the unfertilized ovary and is responsible for the enlargement of the ovary into a fruit, a process known as parthenocarpy.

NAA (1-Naphthaleneacetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) are synthetic auxins, while IBA (Indole-3-butyric acid) is another natural auxin but IAA is the primary one involved in this specific process.

Answer: IAA

71548.subject: Biology
71548.text: Active absorption of water by roots is _____.
options: Along the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of ATP (energy).
Against the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of ATP (energy).
Against the DPD gradient and without the expenditure of ATP (energy).
Along the DPD gradient and without the expenditure of ATP (energy).
71548.sol:
Active absorption of water by roots can be of two types: osmotic and non-osmotic.

In non-osmotic active absorption, water is absorbed against the concentration gradient or DPD (Diffusion Pressure Deficit) gradient. Since the movement of water occurs against the natural gradient (i.e., from a region of higher DPD to a region of lower DPD), it requires the direct expenditure of metabolic energy in the form of ATP.

Therefore, active absorption of water by roots is against the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of ATP.

Answer: Against the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of ATP (energy).

71690.subject: Chemistry
71690.text:
Which of the following acid has the highest acid strength?
(A) Acetic acid
(B) fluoroacetic acid
(C) 4-Nitrobenzoic acid
(D) 4-Methyl Benzoic acid is
71690.sol:
Acid strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base, which increases with the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (-I, -R effects).

In fluoroacetic acid ($F-CH_2-COOH$), the highly electronegative fluorine atom exerts a strong -I effect from the adjacent $\alpha$-carbon, highly stabilizing the conjugate base. Its $pK_a$ is approximately $2.59$.

In 4-nitrobenzoic acid, the $-NO_2$ group exerts both -I and -R effects, but it is located farther away on the benzene ring. Its $pK_a$ is approximately $3.41$.

Acetic acid ($pK_a \approx 4.76$) and 4-methylbenzoic acid ($pK_a \approx 4.34$) have electron-donating groups (+I and hyperconjugation), which decrease acid strength.

Comparing the $pK_a$ values, fluoroacetic acid has the lowest $pK_a$ and is therefore the strongest acid among the given options.

Answer: (B)

71994.subject: Chemistry
71994.text: 13 g nonvolatile solute dissolved in 100 gm of water gives vapour pressure of 27.371 mm Hg at room temperature. Find the molar mass of solute. (vapour pressure of water is 28.065 mm Hg at room temperature)
71994.sol:
Given:
Mass of solute, $w_2 = 13$ g
Mass of solvent (water), $w_1 = 100$ g
Vapour pressure of pure water, $P^0 = 28.065$ mm Hg
Vapour pressure of solution, $P_s = 27.371$ mm Hg
Molar mass of water, $M_1 = 18$ g/mol

Using the formula for relative lowering of vapour pressure (assuming dilute solution):
$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1}$

$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = \dfrac{w_2 \times M_1}{M_2 \times w_1}$

$M_2 = \dfrac{w_2 \times M_1 \times P^0}{w_1 \times (P^0 - P_s)}$

Substituting the given values:
$M_2 = \dfrac{13 \times 18 \times 28.065}{100 \times (28.065 - 27.371)}$

$M_2 = \dfrac{13 \times 18 \times 28.065}{100 \times 0.694}$

$M_2 \approx 94.74$ g/mol

Answer: 94.74 g/mol

72277.subject: Physics
72277.text: The magnetic induction produced at the centre of the air-core solenoid is $B_0$. If the air-core is replaced by an iron-core of susceptibility $\chi$, the magnetic induction is $B_1$. The ratio of $\dfrac{B_1}{B_0}$ is
72277.sol:
The magnetic induction at the centre of an air-core solenoid is given by

$B_0 = \mu_0 n I$

When the air-core is replaced by an iron-core of susceptibility $\chi$, the magnetic induction becomes

$B_1 = \mu n I$

The permeability of the core $\mu$ is related to the relative permeability $\mu_r$ and the permeability of free space $\mu_0$ by

$\mu = \mu_0 \mu_r$

The relative permeability is related to the magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ by

$\mu_r = 1 + \chi$

Substituting this into the expression for $B_1$, we get

$B_1 = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) n I$

The ratio of the magnetic inductions is

$\dfrac{B_1}{B_0} = \dfrac{\mu_0 (1 + \chi) n I}{\mu_0 n I} = 1 + \chi$

Answer: $1 + \chi$

76474.subject: Mathematics
76474.text: What is the sum of the binary numbers $(101101101)_2$ and $(100011)_2$?
76474.sol:
Converting the given binary numbers to decimal:

$(101101101)_2 = 1 \times 2^8 + 0 \times 2^7 + 1 \times 2^6 + 1 \times 2^5 + 0 \times 2^4 + 1 \times 2^3 + 1 \times 2^2 + 0 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0$

$(101101101)_2 = 256 + 0 + 64 + 32 + 0 + 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 365$

$(100011)_2 = 1 \times 2^5 + 0 \times 2^4 + 0 \times 2^3 + 0 \times 2^2 + 1 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0$

$(100011)_2 = 32 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 35$

Adding the decimal values:

Sum $= 365 + 35 = 400$

Converting $400$ back to binary:

$400 = 256 + 128 + 16 = 2^8 + 2^7 + 2^4$

Therefore, $400 = (110010000)_2$

Answer: $(110010000)_2$

76816.subject: Mathematics
76816.text: What is $\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \frac{x}{2}\right) d x$ equal to?
76816.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{I} & =\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \frac{x}{2}\right) d x \qquad \qquad...\mathrm{(i)}\\
\mathrm{I} & =\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\right) d x \\
& =\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\cot \frac{x}{2}\right) d x \qquad \qquad...\mathrm{(ii)}
\end{aligned}$
Adding equation (1) and (2), we get
$2 \mathrm{I}=\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \frac{x}{2}\right) d x+\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\cot \frac{x}{2}\right) d x\begin{aligned} 2 \mathrm{I} & =\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \frac{x}{2} \cot \frac{x}{2}\right) d x \\ 2 \mathrm{I} & =\int_0^\pi \ln \left(\tan \frac{x}{2} \times \frac{1}{\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right) d x \\ \mathrm{I} & =\frac{1}{2} \int_0^\pi \ln (1) d x \quad(\therefore \ln 1=0) \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=0\end{aligned}$

80203.subject: Botany
80203.text: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondrial membrane is not correct ?
options: the outer membrane resembles a sieve
the outer membrane is permeable to all kinds of molecules
the enzymes of the electron transfer chain are embedded in the outer membrane
the inner membrane is highly convoluted forming a series of infoldings
80203.sol:
In mitochondria, the outer membrane is semi permeable, and thus resembles a sieve permeable to all molecules of 10,000 Daltons. The inner membrane is selectively permeable and highly convoluted, forming a series of infoldings known as cristae. The enzymes of the electron transport chain are found in the inner membrane, while the outer membrane contains enzymes involved in mitochondrial lipid synthesis.
Related Theory
The inner membrane surrounds a central fluid-filled space called inner chamber or mitochondrial matrix. The machinery for energy generation can be found on the cristae (infoldings of the inner membrane). The matrix side of the inner membrane and cristae bear numerous tennis racket-like particles called oxysomes or elementary particles or $F_0-F_1$ particles. The cristae and the proteins of the inner membrane aid in the production of ATP molecules during oxidative phosphorylation. Enzymes of electron transport chain are located in the inner membrane.

Now, $\left(\alpha + 1\right)\left(\beta +1\right)\left(\gamma +1\right)$

$= \alpha\beta\gamma + \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha + \alpha + \beta + \gamma +1$

$= 3 + 6 + 5 + 1$

$= 15$

The small oscillation of the bob occur relative to a stationary axis passing through $AB$. The line $CD$ is perpendicular to the axis $AB$. The bob behaves as a simple pendulum of length $CD$ oscillating due to component of its weight $mgcos\theta$.

$⇒ x = 4$

95054.text: Sound waves in the air are always longitudinal because
options: Of the inherent characteristics of sound waves in air
Air does not have a modulus of rigidity
Air is a mixture of several gases
Density of air is very small
95054.sol:
In the transmission of sound through air, there is no actual movement of air from the sound producing body to our ear. The air layers only vibrate back and forth, and transfer the sound energy from one layer to the next layer till it reaches our ear. This back and forth motion causes the compression and rarefaction in a sound wave. This motion is along the direction of propagation of sound and hence, the sound waves are longitudinal. Note that the layers of air consist of molecules of gases. Note that the layers of air consist of molecules of gases. So, when the air layers vibrate back and forth, we actually mean that the molecules in air layers vibrate back and forth by a small distance.

Therefore, it simply means that air does not have modulus of rigidity.

100216.subject: Physics
100216.text: Form the $v - t$ graph shown, the ratio of distance to displacement in $25s$ of motion is:
100216.sol:
The area under the velocity time graph gives the displacement. The area for $t = 0s\text{to}t = 25s$is 

$( Area ) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10\right) + \left(5 \times 10\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 30 \times 5\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5\right)$

 $⇒ Area = 25 + 50 + 75 + 50 - 50 = 150m$
Hence, the displacement $= 150m$

The distance is defined as the path taken by the object to travel from initial to final position. Also note that displacement is a vector quantity, but distance is a scalar quantity.
Distance $= \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10\right) + \left(5 \times 10\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 30 \times 5\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5\right)$
$= ( 200 + 50 ) = 250m$

Therefore, required ratio
$\dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{displacement}} = \dfrac{250}{150} = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

100329.subject: Physics
100329.text: An elevator is accelerating vertically upwards at a rate of $\dfrac{g}{3}$. A person inside the elevator drops a ball from a height $h$ above the elevator floor. What is the time taken for the ball to reach the floor?
100329.sol:
Let the upward direction be positive and downward be negative.

Acceleration of the elevator, $a_{e} = +\dfrac{g}{3}$
Acceleration of the freely falling ball with respect to the ground, $a_{b} = -g$

The relative acceleration of the ball with respect to the elevator is:
$a_{\text{rel}} = a_{b} - a_{e} = -g - \left(+\dfrac{g}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{4g}{3}$
The magnitude of relative acceleration is $\dfrac{4g}{3}$ downwards.

The initial relative velocity of the ball is zero ($u_{\text{rel}} = 0$).
Using the second equation of motion for relative motion:
$s_{\text{rel}} = u_{\text{rel}}t + \dfrac{1}{2}a_{\text{rel}}t^2$
$h = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{4g}{3}\right)t^2$
$h = \dfrac{2g}{3}t^2$
$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{3h}{2g}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{3h}{2g}}$

100390.text: A particle starts from rest and has an acceleration of $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ for $10 \mathrm{sec}$. After that, it travels for $30 \mathrm{sec}$ with constant speed and then undergoes a retardation of $4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and comes back to rest. The total distance covered by the particle is
100390.sol:
Initial velocity $(u)=0$,
Acceleration $\left(a_1\right)=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and time during acceleration $\left(t_1\right)=10 \mathrm{sec}$.
Time during constant velocity $\left(t_2\right)=30 \mathrm{sec}$ and retardation $\left(a_2\right)=-4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ (-ve sign due to retardation). Distance covered by the particle during acceleration,

$\begin{gathered}$s_1=u t_1+$\frac{1}{2}$a_1 t_1^2=(0 $\times$10)+$\frac{1}{2} \times$2 $\times($10)^2 \\
=100 $\mathrm{~m}
\end{gathered}$And velocity of the particle at the end of acceleration,

v=u+a_1 t_1=0+(2 $\times$10)=20 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s} .$Therefore distance covered by the particle during constant velocity $\left(s_2\right)=v \times t_2$
=20 $\times$30=600 $\mathrm{~m}$Relation for the distance covered by the particle during retardation $\left(s_3\right)$ is $v^2=u^2+2 a_2 s_3$
or, $\quad(0)^2=(20)^2+2 \times(-4) \times s_3=400-8 s_3$
or, $s_3=400 / 8=50 \mathrm{~m}$
Therefore total distance covered by the particle

s=s_1+s_2+s_3=100+600+50=750 $\mathrm{~m}$

101048.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
101048.text: A body of mass $m_1$ collides elastically with another body of mass $m_2$ at rest. If the velocity of $m_1$ after collision becomes $2 / 3$ times its initial velocity, the ratio of their masses is
101048.sol:
Let $v$ be the initial velocity of body of mass $m_1$ before collision.
Since collision is elastic both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
$\therefore m_1 v=m_1 \frac{2}{3} v+m_2 v_2 or m_1\left(v-\frac{2}{3} v\right)=m_2 v_2$

Also, $\frac{1}{2} m_1 v^2=\frac{1}{2} m_1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 v^2+\frac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2$ or $m_1\left(v^2-\frac{4}{9} v^2\right)=m_2 v_2^2
or \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}$
Equating (i) and (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}=\frac{3 v_2}{v} \text{$ or $} \frac{v_2}{v}=\frac{5}{3} \\ & \therefore \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{3 \times 5}{3}=\frac{5}{1}\end{aligned}$

102427.subject: Physics
102427.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a particle executing simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$ and time period $T$, the magnitude of its average acceleration from the mean position to the positive extreme position is $\dfrac{8\pi A}{T^2}$.

Reason (R): Average acceleration is the ratio of the total change in velocity to the total time taken, and the velocity changes from $A\omega$ to $0$ in a time interval of $\dfrac{T}{4}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102427.sol:
The Reason statement correctly defines average acceleration as the ratio of total change in velocity to total time taken ($a_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$).

For a particle moving from the mean position to the positive extreme position in SHM:
Initial velocity at the mean position, $v_i = A\omega$
Final velocity at the extreme position, $v_f = 0$
Time taken to travel from mean to extreme, $\Delta t = \dfrac{T}{4}$

Therefore, the Reason is true.

Using these values to calculate average acceleration:
$a_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{v_f - v_i}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0 - A\omega}{\dfrac{T}{4}} = \dfrac{-4A\omega}{T}$

Since $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, we can substitute this into the expression:
$a_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{-4A\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)}{T} = \dfrac{-8\pi A}{T^2}$

The magnitude of the average acceleration is $\dfrac{8\pi A}{T^2}$. Thus, the Assertion is also true.

Since the calculation directly relies on the principles stated in the Reason, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

102516.text: The time period of a simple pendulum is $T$ remaining at rest inside a lift. Find the time period of pendulum when lift starts to move up with an acceleration of $g / 4$.
102516.sol:
When the lift is at rest, the time period of the simple pendulum is $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$
Now, if the lift is moving up with an acceleration $\frac{g}{4}$ then the effective acceleration due to gravity

$\begin{aligned}$& g^{\prime}=g+$\frac{g}{4}=\frac{5 g}{4}$\\
& \therefore $\text{ Time period }$T^{\prime}=2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g^{\prime}}}$\\
&=2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{5 g / 4}}$\\
&=$\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \times$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$T
\end{aligned}

102895.subject: Physics
102895.text: A fixed uniformly charged solid non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ has a total positive charge $Q$. A small particle of mass $m$ and negative charge $-q$ is released from rest at a distance $4R$ from the centre of the sphere. The particle moves towards the sphere under the influence of the electrostatic force. What is the kinetic energy of the particle just before it strikes the surface of the sphere?
102895.sol:
The electrostatic field is conservative, so the mechanical energy of the particle is conserved during its motion.

Let the initial position be at a distance $r_i = 4R$ and the final position be at the surface of the sphere, $r_f = R$.

The electric potential at a distance $r$ ($r \ge R$) from the centre of the sphere is $V(r) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r}$.

The initial potential energy of the system is:
$U_i = -q V(4R) = -q \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{4R} \right) = -\dfrac{qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

The final potential energy of the system just before striking the surface is:
$U_f = -q V(R) = -q \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{R} \right) = -\dfrac{qQ}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

According to the conservation of mechanical energy:
$K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f$

Since the particle is released from rest, $K_i = 0$.

$0 - \dfrac{qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R} = K_f - \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

$K_f = \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R} - \dfrac{qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R} = \dfrac{3qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

The correct option is $\dfrac{3qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3qQ}{16\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

102921.subject: Physics
102921.text: A large spherical liquid drop is charged to a potential of $500\text{ V}$. It breaks up into $N$ identical smaller spherical drops. If the potential of each of the smaller drops is found to be $20\text{ V}$, what is the value of $N$?
102921.sol:
Let the radius of the large drop be $R$ and its charge be $Q$. Its potential is given by $V_{\text{large}} = \dfrac{kQ}{R}$.

When it breaks into $N$ identical smaller drops of radius $r$ and charge $q$, the total charge and total volume are conserved.
Charge conservation: $Q = Nq$
Volume conservation: $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = N \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \Rightarrow R = N^{1/3}r$

The potential of each small drop is $V_{\text{small}} = \dfrac{kq}{r}$.

Taking the ratio of the potentials:
$\dfrac{V_{\text{large}}}{V_{\text{small}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{kQ}{R}}{\dfrac{kq}{r}} = \left(\dfrac{Q}{q}\right)\left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right) = (N)\left(\dfrac{1}{N^{1/3}}\right) = N^{2/3}$

Given $V_{\text{large}} = 500\text{ V}$ and $V_{\text{small}} = 20\text{ V}$:
$N^{2/3} = \dfrac{500}{20} = 25$

Solving for $N$:
$N = (25)^{3/2} = (5^2)^{3/2} = 5^3 = 125$

Answer: $125$

103147.text:
A circuit is connected to a $24\text{ V}$ battery. The circuit consists of $C_1 = 6\ \mu\text{F}$ and $C_2 = 3\ \mu\text{F}$ connected in series. This series combination is connected in parallel with $C_3 = 2\ \mu\text{F}$. Finally, this entire parallel block is connected in series with $C_4 = 4\ \mu\text{F}$. Match the physical quantities in List-I with their numerical values in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Equivalent capacitance of the circuit(I) $4\text{ V}$
(B) Charge on capacitor $C_4$(II) $2\ \mu\text{F}$
(C) Potential difference across $C_1$(III) $48\ \mu\text{C}$
(D) Charge on capacitor $C_3$(IV) $24\ \mu\text{C}$
103147.sol:
The equivalent capacitance of $C_1$ and $C_2$ in series is $C_{12} = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = 2\ \mu\text{F}$.

This combination is in parallel with $C_3 = 2\ \mu\text{F}$, so the equivalent capacitance of the parallel block is $C_{123} = 2 + 2 = 4\ \mu\text{F}$.

The parallel block is in series with $C_4 = 4\ \mu\text{F}$. The total equivalent capacitance of the circuit is $C_{eq} = \dfrac{4 \times 4}{4 + 4} = 2\ \mu\text{F}$. This matches (A) with (II).

The total charge drawn from the battery is $Q_{total} = C_{eq} \times V = 2\ \mu\text{F} \times 24\text{ V} = 48\ \mu\text{C}$.
Since $C_4$ is in series with the rest of the circuit, the charge on $C_4$ is the total charge, $48\ \mu\text{C}$. This matches (B) with (III).

The potential difference across $C_4$ is $V_4 = \dfrac{Q_4}{C_4} = \dfrac{48\ \mu\text{C}}{4\ \mu\text{F}} = 12\text{ V}$.
The potential difference across the parallel block is $V_{123} = 24\text{ V} - 12\text{ V} = 12\text{ V}$.

The charge on $C_3$ is $Q_3 = C_3 \times V_{123} = 2\ \mu\text{F} \times 12\text{ V} = 24\ \mu\text{C}$. This matches (D) with (IV).

The charge on the series branch containing $C_1$ and $C_2$ is $Q_{12} = C_{12} \times V_{123} = 2\ \mu\text{F} \times 12\text{ V} = 24\ \mu\text{C}$.
Since $C_1$ and $C_2$ are in series, the charge on $C_1$ is $24\ \mu\text{C}$.
The potential difference across $C_1$ is $V_1 = \dfrac{Q_1}{C_1} = \dfrac{24\ \mu\text{C}}{6\ \mu\text{F}} = 4\text{ V}$. This matches (C) with (I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

As we know that, potential energy of a magnet in a magnetic field
$\begin{aligned} U & =-\mathbf{m} \cdot \mathbf{B} \\ & =-m B \cos \theta\end{aligned}$
where, $m=$ magnetic dipole moment of the magnet $B=$ magnetic field
Case I $\theta=180^{\circ}$

$=m B \quad\left[\because \cos 180^{\circ}=-1\right]$
Case II $\theta=90^{\circ}$
$U_2=0 \quad\left[\because \cos 90^{\circ}=0\right]$
Case III $\theta$ is acute angle
$\begin{aligned} & & \in\left(0,90^{\circ}\right) \\ \therefore & \cos \theta & =\text{ positive } \\ \text{ Thus, } & U_3 & =\text{ negative }\end{aligned}$
Case IV $\theta$ is obtuse
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & & \theta \in\left(90^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}\right) \\ \therefore \quad & \cos \in(0,-1)\end{array}$
Thus, $\quad U_4=$ positive
Therefore, decreasing order of $P E$ is
I $\gt$ IV $\gt$ II $\gt$ III

107734.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Lewis structure of $CO_{2}$ having two double bonds is more stable than the Lewis structure having one single bond and one triple bond.
Reason (R): The formal charge on the central carbon atom is zero in both of these Lewis structures.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
107734.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The most stable Lewis structure is the one where the formal charges on the atoms are minimized (closest to zero). In the structure with two double bonds ($O=C=O$), the formal charge on all atoms (both C and O) is zero. In the structure with one single and one triple bond ($O \equiv C - O$), the formal charges are $+1$ on the triple-bonded oxygen, $-1$ on the single-bonded oxygen, and $0$ on carbon. Thus, the structure with two double bonds has lower formal charges and is more stable.

Reason (R) is true: The formal charge on carbon in $O=C=O$ is $4 - 0 - \dfrac{8}{2} = 0$. The formal charge on carbon in $O \equiv C - O$ is also $4 - 0 - \dfrac{8}{2} = 0$.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The correct explanation for the greater stability of the double-bonded structure is the minimization of formal charges on the oxygen atoms, not the carbon atom (which has a formal charge of zero in both cases).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

114909.subject: Chemistry
114909.text: For a first-order reaction, the plot of $\log[R]$ against time ($t$ in seconds) yields a straight line with a slope of $-3.01 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}$. The half-life of the reaction is:
114909.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate equation is:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log\dfrac{[R]_0}{[R]}$

Rearranging this equation gives:

$\log[R] = -\dfrac{k}{2.303}t + \log[R]_0$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, the slope ($m$) of the plot of $\log[R]$ versus $t$ is $-\dfrac{k}{2.303}$.

Given slope $= -3.01 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}$

$-\dfrac{k}{2.303} = -3.01 \times 10^{-3}$

$k = 2.303 \times 3.01 \times 10^{-3} = 6.93 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}$

The half-life ($t_{1/2}$) for a first-order reaction is:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k} = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93 \times 10^{-3}} = 100 \text{ s}$

Answer: $100 \text{ s}$

119878.subject: Chemistry
119878.text:
Identify the major product $C$ formed in the following sequence of reactions:
$\text{Benzamide} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}} A \xrightarrow[\text{273-278 K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} B \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O, warm}} C$
119878.sol:
Benzamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation with $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to form aniline ($A$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \ (A)$

Aniline reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$) at 273-278 K to undergo diazotization, forming benzene diazonium chloride ($B$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{273-278 K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-} \ (B)$

Warming the stable aromatic diazonium salt with water hydrolyses it to yield phenol ($C$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O, warm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \ (C) + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, the major product $C$ is phenol.

Benzene diazonium chloride is the intermediate $B$, not the final product. Bromobenzene would be formed if the Sandmeyer reaction ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Br}_2/\text{HBr}$) was used. Benzyl alcohol is incorrect as the carbon skeleton has lost a carbon atom in the first step.

Answer: Phenol

120996.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the denaturation of proteins:
I. Denaturation can be caused by physical changes like temperature or chemical changes like pH.
II. During this process, the uncoiling of helix and unfolding of globule takes place.
III. The primary structure of the protein is altered during the coagulation of egg white on boiling.
IV. Denaturation leads to the loss of biological activity of the protein.

How many of the given statements are correct?
120996.sol:
Statement I is correct: Denaturation is caused by physical changes (such as heating) or chemical changes (such as a change in pH) that disrupt the native conformation of the protein.

Statement II is correct: Denaturation involves the unfolding of globules and uncoiling of helices, which destroys the secondary and tertiary structures.

Statement III is incorrect: The coagulation of egg white on boiling is an example of denaturation. During denaturation, the primary structure remains intact and is not altered.

Statement IV is correct: The structural changes during denaturation lead to the loss of biological activity of the protein.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

122074.subject: Botany
options: manufactures food for itself, as well as for the gametophyte
is partially parasitic on the gametophyte
produces gametes that give rise to the gametophyte
arises from a spore produced from the gametophyte
122074.sol:
In mosses, the sporophyte developing from the embryo partially depends on the gametophyte. It contains chlorophyll and hence is capable of making its own food. Sporophyte is attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte so that it can get nourishment from the gametophyte. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo meiosis to produce haploid spores. The spores germinate to produce gametophyte.
Related Theory
When a moss spore germinates it first develops a protonema (sporophyte), a filamentous to sheet-like growth form. the leaves develop on the stems, giving rise to one or more leafy-stemmed plants. The protonema are ephemeral, with the leafy-stemmed plants the persistent and dominant growth form. The leafy-stemmed part is the gametophyte. because it produces gametes. Sex organs are multicellular. Male sex organ is called antheridium and produces biflagellate antherozoids. The female sex organ is called archegonium and produces a single egg.

123808.subject: Botany
123808.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
A.Prophasei.Centromeres split and chromatids separate
B.Metaphaseii.Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements
C.Anaphaseiii.Initiation of the assembly of mitotic spindle
D.Telophaseiv.Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123808.sol:
The correct matching of the stages of mitosis with their defining events is as follows:

Prophase (A) is characterised by the initiation of the assembly of the mitotic spindle (iii).

Metaphase (B) is defined by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator and the attachment of spindle fibres to the kinetochores of chromosomes (iv).

Anaphase (C) is marked by the splitting of centromeres and the separation of chromatids, which then move to opposite poles (i).

Telophase (D) is the final stage where chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and lose their discrete identity as the nuclear envelope reforms (ii).

Therefore, the correct matching code is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

Answer: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii

Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful study that the complexity in organ and organ systems displays certain discernable trend. This discernable trend is called evolutionary trend (You will study the details in class XII). In this chapter, you are being introduced to morphology and anatomy of frog. Morphology refers to study of form or externally visible features. In the case of plants or microbes, the term morphology precisely means only this. In case of animals this refers to the external appearance of the organs or parts of the body. The word anatomy conventionally is used for the study of morphology of internal organs in the animals. 129514.subject: Zoology
129514.text: What is the process of ultrafiltration?
options: The process of filtering blood through the glomerular capillary blood pressure
The process of filtering blood so finely through membranes, that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass onto the lumen of the Bowman’s capsule
The process of filtering plasma through the glomerular capillary blood pressure
The process of filtering urine through the glomerular capillary blood pressure
129514.sol: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration. On an average, 1100-1200 ml of blood is filtered by the kidneys per minute which constitute roughly 1/5th of the blood pumped out by each ventricle of the heart in a minute. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman’s capsule and a basement membrane between these two layers. The epithelial cells of Bowman’s capsule called podocytes are arranged in an intricate manner so as to leave some minute spaces called filtration slits or slit pores. Blood is filtered so finely through these membranes, that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass onto the lumen of the Bowman’s capsule. Therefore, it is considered as a process of ultra filtration.

Read the following statement and select the correct statement
1. Human beings have a significant ability to maintain and moderate the respiratory rhythm to suit the demands of the body tissues
2. A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation.
3. Receptors associated with aortic arch and renal artery also can recognise changes in CO2 and H+ concentration and send necessary signals to the rhythm centre for remedial actions.
4. The role of oxygen in the regulation of respiratory rhythm is quite significant.
5. Neural signal from pneumotaxic centre can reduce the duration of inspiration and thereby alter the respiratory rate.
130002.sol: Human beings have a significant ability to maintain and moderate the respiratory rhythm to suit the demands of the body tissues. This is done by the neural system. A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation. Another centre present in the pons region of the brain called pneumotaxic centre can moderate the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre. Neural signal from this centre can reduce the duration of inspiration and thereby alter the respiratory rate. A chemosensitive area is situated adjacent to the rhythm centre which is highly sensitive to CO2 and hydrogen ions. Increase in these substances can activate this centre, which in turn can signal the rhythm centre to make necessary adjustments in the respiratory process by which these substances can be eliminated. Receptors associated with aortic arch and carotid artery also can recognise changes in CO2 and H+ concentration and send necessary signals to the rhythm centre for remedial actions. The role of oxygen in the regulation of respiratory rhythm is quite insignificant.

130747.subject: Zoology
130747.text: Which of the following options correctly identifies the contraceptive method, its category, and its corresponding mechanism of action?
options: Cervical caps - Barrier method - Inhibits ovulation
Coitus interruptus - Natural method - Prevents spermatogenesis
Copper T - Barrier method - Suppresses sperm motility
Tubectomy - Surgical method - Blocks gamete transport
130747.sol:
Tubectomy is a surgical method (sterilisation) in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up. This blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception.

Cervical caps are barrier methods but they do not inhibit ovulation; they prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix.

Coitus interruptus is a natural method that prevents insemination by withdrawal of the penis just before ejaculation, but it does not halt spermatogenesis.

Copper T suppresses sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms, but it is an Intra Uterine Device (IUD), not a barrier method.

Answer: Tubectomy - Surgical method - Blocks gamete transport

131467.subject: Zoology
131467.text: What did Hershey and Chase use to determine the genetic material of bacteriophages?
131467.sol: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages. The bacteriophage attaches to the bacteria and its genetic material then enters the bacterial cell. The bacterial cell treats the viral genetic material as if it was its own and subsequently manufactures more virus particles. Hershey and Chase worked to discover whether it was protein or DNA from the viruses that entered the bacteria. They grew some viruses on a medium that contained radioactive phosphorus and some others on a medium that contained radioactive sulfur. Viruses grown in the presence of radioactive phosphorus contained radioactive DNA but not radioactive protein because DNA contains phosphorus but protein does not. Similarly, viruses grown on radioactive sulfur contained radioactive protein but not radioactive DNA because DNA does not contain sulfur.

131506.subject: Zoology
131506.text: What is the role of a terminator in a transcription unit?
options: To initiate the process of transcription
To define the boundaries of the region of DNA that would be transcribed
To mark the end of the segment of DNA that would be transcribed
To prevent RNA from being translated into protein
131506.sol: The promoter and terminator flank the structural gene in a transcription unit. The promoter is said to be located towards the 5' -end (upstream) of the structural gene (the reference is made with respect to the polarity of the coding strand). It is a DNA sequence that provides binding site for RNA polymerase, and it is the presence of a promoter in a transcription unit that also defines the template and coding strands. By switching its position with terminator, the definition of coding and template strands could be reversed. The terminator is located towards the 3' -end (downstream) of the coding strand and it usually defines the end of the process of transcription (Figure 5.9). There are additional regulatory sequences that may be present further upstream or downstream to the promoter. Some of the properties of these sequences shall be discussed while dealing with regulation of gene expression.

131585.subject: Zoology
131585.text: What is the function of the transacetylase gene in the lac operon?
options: It is not involved in lactose metabolism
131585.sol: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene – here the term i does not refer to inducer, rather it is derived from the word inhibitor) and three structural genes (z, y, and a). The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides. The gene encodes a transacetylase. Hence, all the three gene products in lac operon are required for metabolism of lactose. In most other operons as well, the genes present in the operon are needed together to function in the same or related metabolic pathway
